# FAQ-029 Engineering FAQ #29

Revision: Rev A

Q: What is the correct target billet temperature setting for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01), and why is this specific temperature used?
A: The target billet temperature for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 1235 °C. Background: this target is the process setpoint used to achieve the metallurgical state required for downstream machining and forging. Rationale: setting the heater to 1235 °C ensures the billet reaches a uniform temperature profile that supports predictable material flow and surface condition during machining. Example application: verify that billets reach and hold 1235 °C prior to transfer to the machining station; if billets do not achieve the specified temperature, follow troubleshooting steps in SOP-P1-L3-03. Records to keep: log the heater setpoint, operator confirmation that billets reached 1235 °C, and any corrective actions taken. Reference procedures: consult SB-1037 for process validation data and SOP-P1-L3-03 for in-shift operator steps.

Q: What is the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02), and what actions should be taken if the limit is approached?
A: The system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 295 bar. Background: this limit is the maximum allowable system pressure for safe operation and component life management. Rationale: operating at or below 295 bar reduces risk of hydraulic component overstress and maintains predictable press performance. Example scenario: if system pressure indications trend toward 295 bar during a production cycle, pause loading and follow the pressure-relief and inspection steps outlined in SOP-P1-L3-03. Records to keep: pressure readouts, time-stamped operator notes indicating when pressure reached a critical level, and any maintenance or adjustments performed. Reference procedures: see SB-1038 for hydraulic maintenance history and SOP-P1-L3-03 for operator response steps.

Q: What lubricant part number is specified for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03), and what are the handling and documentation expectations?
A: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is CFW-LUB-526. Background: this lubricant was validated for compatibility with shot blast cabinet components and the heat-treat environment. Rationale: using CFW-LUB-526 avoids chemical incompatibilities and reduces wear on bearings and linkage. Example procedure: when replenishing or reapplying lubricant to EQ-P3-L4-SB03, use only CFW-LUB-526 and follow the application method in SB-1037. Records to keep: part number used, quantity applied, batch or lot identifier from the lubricant container, and the name of the person performing application. Reference procedures: SB-1037 contains approved lubricants list and handling notes; SOP-P1-L3-03 contains application checkpoint items.

Q: What lubricant part number is specified for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03), and how should deviations be handled?
A: The lubricant part number for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is CFW-LUB-725. Background: CFW-LUB-725 was selected after compatibility testing with induction heater seals and conveyors. Rationale: using the specified lubricant maintains equipment reliability and prevents contamination of machining processes. Example of deviation management: if CFW-LUB-725 is not available, do not substitute without an approved deviation. Initiate the documented deviation request and reference SB-1038 for historical approvals. Records to keep: lubricant part number applied, justification for any deviation request, approval record, and post-deviation inspection notes. Reference procedures: consult SB-1038 for past deviation outcomes and SOP-P1-L3-03 for routine lubrication checkpoints.

Q: What lubricant part number is specified for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01), and what inspection and recordkeeping practices are required?
A: The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is CFW-LUB-938. Background: CFW-LUB-938 is approved for ring rolling support equipment where specific high-temperature-compatible lubricants are required. Rationale: using CFW-LUB-938 minimizes bearing failures and preserves surface finish critical to ring rolling feed mechanisms. Example inspection practice: after lubricant application, inspect linkage points and record visual condition and any abnormalities in the equipment log. Records to keep: lubricant part number and batch identifier, date and time of application, inspector/operator initials, and any corrective actions taken. Reference procedures: SB-1037 lists approved lubricants and inspection checkpoints; SOP-P1-L3-03 details the log format and mandatory fields.

Related documents: SB-1037, SB-1038, SOP-P1-L3-03.
